children: Canada’s 10-year government bond yield settled near 3.94% in mid-September after falling as low as 3.87% on lower oil prices.
The yield then rose following the Federal Reserve’s rate hike, as the Fed raised the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 bps to 3.75%-4%.
Updated Fed projections showed that most policymakers expect another hike before the end of 2026.
The Bank of Canada kept its key policy rate unchanged at 2.25% at its September meeting, as widely expected.
However, it noted that inflation risks had increased, while new tariffs had made the growth outlook more uncertain.
Governor Macklem said policymakers were prepared to raise rates if inflation remained elevated.
Still, a halt in the oil rally following reports of a potential recovery of Saudi Arabia’s key East-West pipeline helped to slow global yields.

title: Canada 10-Year Yield Nears 3.94%
